name: LinkedIn: Company
summary: Open a LinkedIn company page read-only and return one merged record: About fields, employee breakdown charts, employee growth, and recent posts.
description: Open a LinkedIn company page once, then click through its own About / People / Posts tabs the way a person would, and return a single merged company record. Covers the About panel (overview text, website, industry, company size, headquarters, founded, specialties, associated members, location count), the People tab breakdown charts (what they do, where they live, where they studied, with each bucket's share of associated members), the employee growth percentage from the home tab, exact follower count, related company pages, and the most recent posts with permalinks and engagement counts. Read-only: never follows, likes, comments, or applies. Use linkedin_company_jobs for the full job listing and hiring-location picture.

company.description: A LinkedIn company slug (e.g. stripe) OR a full https://www.linkedin.com/company/<slug>/ URL.

max_posts.description: Maximum number of recent posts to return. Defaults to 10. Hard cap 50.

steps.name: Merge the home, About, People, and Posts data into one company record

help.summary: Open a LinkedIn company page and return About fields, employee breakdown charts, growth percentage, and recent posts as one record.

parameters.company: A LinkedIn company slug (e.g. stripe) OR a full /company/<slug>/ URL.
parameters.max_posts: Maximum recent posts to return (default 10, cap 50).

examples.description: Return the full company record for Stripe with the 10 most recent posts.
Same, passing a full company URL and asking for 25 posts.

returns: { company_url, slug, company_id, name, tagline, followers, employee_growth, about, website, industry, company_size, headquarters, founded, specialties, company_type, phone, verified_page, locations_count, associated_members, what_they_do[], where_they_live[], where_they_studied[], what_they_studied[], skills[], posts_fetched, posts_last_30_days, posts[], related_companies[], jobs_search_url }
Breakdown arrays are formatted "<label> — <count> (<share>%)" where the share is that bucket's percentage of associated_members.
notes: Read-only. Never follows, likes, comments, reposts, or applies.
Loads the company page once, then clicks its own About / People / Posts tabs instead of re-navigating, so the traffic pattern looks like a person browsing.
company_id is the numeric LinkedIn organisation id, scraped from the page's own f_C jobs link. Feed it to linkedin_company_jobs, or use jobs_search_url directly.
employee_growth is the free 'Growth trends' percentage on the company home tab. The deeper hiring-trend chart is LinkedIn Premium only and is not scraped.

LinkedIn does not publish a lifetime post count. posts_fetched is how many were loaded and posts_last_30_days is how many of those were posted within 30 days, which is the usable posting-cadence signal.
The company About tab is the classic UI with real dt/dd pairs, so those fields are stable. Missing fields degrade to empty string, empty array, or 0.
Every execute_javascript step sets use_cdp_eval because LinkedIn's CSP blocks script-tag injection on all pages.
Intermediate tab data is stashed in sessionStorage under __rzn_co_* keys so it survives the tab-to-tab navigations, then merged in the final step.
